rules.statement: Do not invent content. Text, data, claims, features, people, quotes, logos and numbers that a person will read as fact ship only if the request, the approved layout or the existing page contains them; content already on a page does not exempt proof and claims from DEC-5. A request covers only its own content: placeholder rows or invented items inside a requested block are unrequested; a marked slot that DEC-5 requires for missing prices or terms is not an invented item. Approval of a direction, a discussion or a reference unlocks proposals, not implementation. Each invented item in a delivered result is a finding; repeating it after a correction raises its severity. This rule is never a reason to remove parts of an existing page, such as its navigation, footer, actions, sections, illustrations or motifs; on an existing page, new elements, sections and decoration are proposed, not added (US-002). The visual treatment of requested content (type, color, motion, an illustration of the product) is design work judged by the interface rules, not by this one; sample data inside a product illustration is not a claim unless it presents customers, quotes or results as real. Not a finding: text the user supplied verbatim; the navigation, footer and primary action that a page of the requested kind needs, when their labels claim nothing the request lacks. Proposals and execution follow US-002.
rules.title: Ship only requested content

rules.statement: Follow the user's current explicit requirements when they differ from general style preferences. Review how well the requested design works and how it uses the project's design system. Do not reject an intentional choice merely because it appears in a generic anti-pattern list.
rules.title: Explicit requirements outrank generic style lists

rules.statement: When the agent believes an element outside the request is needed, it sends a separate proposal with the element's purpose and a preview instead of adding it to the result (UR-1). Inside the authorized scope, technical steps, checks and fixes of defects against the stated intent are done without asking, and signals such as risks, contradictions or lost elements are raised without asking. Outside that scope, or when a step is irreversible or external, the agent reports and asks first.
rules.title: Needed additions are proposed; execution is proactive

rules.statement: Before presenting a revision, verify the actual result against its requirements. Check design-system use, behavior and visual output separately. Reading guidelines or passing a build is not evidence that the interface meets its acceptance criteria. Use an independent reviewer before handoff. The reviewer gets the result and the original requirement, not the author's plan or explanations, and judges what is on screen. A finding is backed by a screenshot of the state it describes; a pass or a failure that is only expected, not seen, is not evidence. Each theme the product supports, such as light and dark, is checked on its own: a pass in one theme does not prove another. For a change to a page, take screenshots at 1440 and 390 pixels wide before the first edit and again after the last, compare them and look for overlap, clipped or lost content and lost character; scroll the page before a full-page screenshot so content that appears on scroll is shown, keep the screenshots next to the result, and list every visible difference between before and after: each one is in the element table with its defect, or it is reverted; a page made from scratch is checked on its final screenshots at both widths; without a browser, the report says the visual check was not done and does not call the work done.
rules.title: Verify the actual result before handoff

rules.statement: Make a systemic fix in the governing design-system component, token or recipe. Use its existing API or a defined extension, then verify the consuming interfaces. Do not conceal a local override behind a new token name.
rules.title: Fix systemic issues at the design-system source

rules.statement: A change to the design system does not by itself require renewed permission for work the user has already authorized. Ask when an unresolved product or design choice needs the owner's decision, and stay within the authorized scope.
rules.title: Design-system changes inside authorized work

rules.statement: Keep a project's visual recipes scoped to that project. Reuse the principle of consistency without turning a particular color, shape or treatment into a universal requirement.
rules.title: Visual recipes stay project-scoped

rules.statement: Preserve the provenance of examples, references and claimed results. Distinguish a recorded example from a live verified run, and an agent proposal from an owner-approved decision. State missing evidence explicitly.
rules.title: Keep provenance of examples and claims

rules.statement: Preserve approved content, behavior and composition outside the requested change. Compare the original requirement, the baseline and the candidate. Treat unverified areas as unknown rather than passed.
rules.title: Leave everything outside the change intact

rules.statement: When asked to remove a pattern throughout a product, locate and update every occurrence in the agreed scope. Verify the affected routes and components before handoff instead of fixing only the example that was pointed out.
rules.title: Product-wide removal covers every occurrence

rules.statement: A page that existed before the current task is the approved baseline for an audit or a fix of it (US-001, US-008). The typefaces, palette, motifs and motion it uses consistently, meaning the same treatment for the same role in two or more places or a reused class, token or component, count as its design system only where one of these rules makes an exception for the approved design system: decoration (DEC-1), lines (DEC-2), labels above headings (DEC-7), monospace type (KR-19), decorative gradients and glow (DEC-9) and the letter case of headings, labels and buttons (ST-5). Every other rule applies as written, with its own counter-examples. Only what is already on the page counts: the agent does not declare signatures, and an element it added, a one-off or an inconsistent use is judged by the rule as written. The baseline protects an element only while it passes the role test of US-012: it does a job for the reader here, such as marking a real sequence, a state or the product's own idea (a motif is the product's own when it depicts what the product is or does, such as a route line for a map app; a generic shape, square or color accent is not), and no more fitting element would do that job better. Repetition alone does not pass the test: decoration that does no job, or whose job a more fitting element would do better, is fixed under US-012 however consistently it repeats, and a treatment that matches the Example of the rule it would be exempt from never enters the baseline. The product's own logo or mark is not fabricated proof and stays as it is, whatever it looks like, even a letter in a square (ST-13, US-012); a contrast, size or touch-target defect on it is fixed by restyling the mark, not by replacing or removing it. The letter case the page uses consistently for headings, labels, buttons or menu items is kept the same way (ST-5); the Example of ST-5 does not exclude it from the baseline, and prose stays under C-11. A page generated in the current task is not a baseline. The baseline never covers these always-findings, which stay findings on any page and are fixed, not only reported: fabricated proof and numbers (DEC-5); a sparkle, wand or gradient chip as a generic sign of AI (ST-2; the product's own registered icon excepted); claims about competitors without a verified source (XP-22b); agent or process service notes (US-009); placeholder or service text (XP-33); text contrast below WCAG AA, 4.5:1 or 3:1 for large text (DEC-6, XP-18), and input boundaries or icons below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11); text too small to read on a phone, such as body text below 14px, where text that carries information inside an illustration, such as map or axis labels, counts at its rendered size; touch targets smaller than KR-3 allows. The page's selling copy is never on this list (US-013). How to fix: the content items of that list (proof and numbers, the AI sign, competitor claims, service notes, placeholder text) are removed or replaced; restyling one is not a fix. Contrast, size and touch-target defects are restyled (US-012). A fabricated item stays only when the user supplies its source; the one case that waits for the user's answer is the one DEC-5 names. How to check: before judging, list the always-findings and the generic tells and keep them out of the baseline; then list every other element the page uses consistently, each with the places it repeats, and apply an exception only to listed elements. A report that keeps an always-finding as part of the system, or leaves it as an open question, is a finding. Example: a landing page whose monospace captions and plain-text section kickers repeat across its sections keeps them (KR-19, DEC-7), and a pricing page for a map app keeps its route-line motif across hero, badge and call to action, while an invented "2,400+ teams" is fixed and a "NEW" badge above the headline keeps its words with its layout fixed (US-013), and "01/"–"04/" on a list of contact links are replaced by icons that say where each link goes (US-012). Not a finding: keeping a consistent pattern that the baseline list names, when it is neither an always-finding nor a generic tell.
rules.title: An existing page is the approved baseline

rules.statement: Fix a defect by changing how the element looks or behaves: its contrast, size, spacing, a shadow or color token, the bounds of its motion, its reduced-motion state. Remove an element only when the element itself is the defect, or when the user asked to remove it. Role test, for every decorative element on any page and for every element a fix would touch: name the job it does for the reader here. If it does none, or a more fitting element would do that job better for the reader, it is itself the defect: replace it with that element, or with the plainer page only when no element is needed for that job, as with a background grid that marks nothing; a removal names what does the element's job now. If it already is the most fitting option, it stays. A replacement names what the old element does wrong for the reader; one that does the same job worse is a finding, and so is a second decorative element that repeats a job another element already does, such as a tinted tile behind an icon. A working icon, mark or illustration with no named defect stays as it is, and an icon that supports a label is not a repeat. The content always-findings of US-011, such as fabricated proof, a service note or placeholder text, and on a page made in the task a pill above the H1 (DEC-7), are such defects: they are removed or replaced, and restyling them is not a fix. A visual fix applies in the same way to every element of the same group, or to none of them: removing the border of one link in a list and keeping the borders of the others is a finding. For content the group is every claim of the same kind on the page, such as all customer names, all quotes or all metrics: every fabricated item in it is fixed, not some, and items with a source stay. Size, weight, letter-spacing, typeface, color, radius, shadow, timing and layout change only to remove a named defect; such a change without one is a finding. When the task is to fix slop rather than to redesign, a visible change needs a defect a visitor would notice, named in plain words next to its rule ID; a change that a reviewer of the before and after cannot tie to such a defect, such as a recolored avatar, bolder text or a new button shape, is a finding and is reverted. On a page that existed before the task, the product's logo is never replaced or removed in such a task, even a weak one, and a glow or gradient the page already has stays unless it causes a defect a visitor would notice; a new mark is only proposed. Contrast is fixed with the smallest change, a text color for the role that fails (a role-scoped text token where accent-colored text fails, at the token's source when it is shared, US-004), not a shift of the brand accent or the palette across the page. How to check: for each changed element, name the defect by rule ID and the smallest change that removes it; a removal that a restyle would have fixed is a finding, and so is any loss without a named reason. The work is not done until it ends with a table that covers every element that changed: element, kept / changed / removed, and the rule ID behind each change. This holds whether the page changed through a plan or directly; a change missing from the table, or listed without a rule ID, is a finding. Example: numbers "01/"–"04/" on a list of contact links replaced by icons that say where each link goes; a background grid that marks nothing replaced by the plain background; 10px captions raised to a readable size and kept in their typeface; a muted text color darkened until it reaches 4.5:1 instead of removing the text; every row of a link list changed the same way. Not a finding: keeping the page's selling copy word for word while fixing its layout (US-013); numbered steps of a real process keeping their numbers; a product's own motif or logo kept; a working icon kept when no better one is named; removing fabricated testimonials (DEC-5); removing an element the user asked to remove.
rules.title: Restyle first, remove last

rules.statement: On a page that existed before the task, its selling copy stays word for word: an announcement of a new feature such as "NEW · …", trial and pricing terms such as "Start free for 14 days", "No credit card", the integrations it names and concrete benefit lines. Removing it, cutting it or replacing it with weaker or vaguer words is a very heavy finding, heavier than the defect it was meant to fix. Fix how it looks or breaks (wrap, size, contrast, spacing), never the words. This rule does not cover fabricated testimonials, client logos or metrics, which DEC-5 judges. On a page made from scratch, prices and terms the request does not give are marked slots (DEC-5). How to check: list every line of the page that sells (announcements, offers, terms, integrations, benefits) before the first edit and compare it word for word with the result. Example: a "NEW · Taskflow now reads your Slack threads" badge that overflows at 390 is restyled so it wraps, and its words stay; "Start free for 14 days" and "No credit card" stay next to the call to action. Not a finding: fixing the layout of that badge; removing a fabricated testimonial (DEC-5).
rules.title: Keep the page's selling copy
